developer-tooling.title: Attribute every adjudication verdict to a reviewer and a time
developer-tooling.description: learn.record() stores a verdict as the bare string 'true_positive' or 'false_positive:note' in Knowledge.adjudicated, with no reviewer, no per-verdict timestamp and no record of which entry point it arrived through. Only the rule carries first_seen/last_seen. The ledger refuses re-adjudication, so a wrong or machine-written mark is permanent and, today, untraceable: there is no way to find whose marks to distrust. The rule that verdicts come from a person is enforced in assistant instructions, not in the code. This matters more now that agents hold shell access and more again if a second person ever adjudicates.
acceptance_criteria: Knowledge.adjudicated holds a structured record carrying verdict reviewer timestamp and entry point rather than a bare string/KNOWLEDGE_VERSION is raised and from_dict migrates a version 1 ledger without losing any existing verdict/record() requires a reviewer identity and refuses to write without one/the reviewer is resolved from an explicit flag or git config user rather than defaulted silently/a test asserts a version 1 ledger round-trips through the new schema/a test asserts a verdict without a reviewer is refused
risk_notes: The ledger is committed and feeds version_hash() so the schema change moves the knowledge version and any pinned scan must be re-pinned/The live ledger has zero adjudications so migration is untested against real data and should be tested against a synthetic version 1 file/Attribution records who not whether they were human and must not be described as proof of personhood

developer-tooling.title: Refuse an adjudication verdict from a non-interactive session
developer-tooling.description: Nothing distinguishes a verdict typed by a person from one written by a script or an agent. review_ui._getch() falls back to input() when raw terminal mode is unavailable, nothing calls isatty(), and cli.cmd_feedback records a verdict from a fully non-interactive invocation. review --apply reads marks from a markdown file, so anything that can write markdown can adjudicate. This is no barrier against a determined caller and is not claimed to be one; it stops the accidental case, which is a piped script, a CI job or an agent shelling out.
acceptance_criteria: the interactive adjudication paths require stdin to be a terminal and refuse otherwise with a reason/the refusal names an explicit override flag so a deliberate batch import is possible and visible/an overridden verdict is recorded with an entry point that says it was not interactive/docs/calibration.md states plainly that this is a guard against accident and not proof of personhood/a test asserts a piped non-interactive feedback invocation is refused
risk_notes: Depends on REQ-020 for the entry point field so it should land after it/An override flag that is easy to pass is an override an agent can pass so the value is the record it leaves not the obstacle it creates/Existing tests that record verdicts programmatically will need the override or a direct call to record()

developer-tooling.title: Declare adapter probe scope deliberately and say what a partial scan does not run
developer-tooling.description: adapters.register_adapters constructs every adapter-backed Probe without a scope argument, so all five external analyzers inherit the repo default from Probe and are recorded as not-assessed in any partial scan. The default is right because nothing has established that ruff bandit checkov semgrep or gitleaks give subset-exact answers on a file subset, but it is inherited rather than chosen. docs/ci.md explains file and repo scope carefully and never names the external analyzers; RUNNING-ON-YOUR-OWN-CODE.md describes the pull-request job without saying it runs native probes only. A reader of either document would reasonably believe their gate runs semgrep. It does not.
acceptance_criteria: every adapter manifest declares its scope explicitly/register_adapters passes the declared scope instead of relying on the Probe default/docs/ci.md names the five external analyzers as repo-scoped and says a partial scan does not run them/RUNNING-ON-YOUR-OWN-CODE.md says the same where it describes the pull-request job/a test asserts no adapter-backed probe relies on the inherited default
risk_notes: Declaring any adapter file-scoped would assert subset-exactness that has never been measured so every declaration must stay repo until evidence exists/This is a documentation and deliberateness change and must not be described as making partial scans cover more

developer-tooling.title: Exercise the Windows code paths in CI
developer-tooling.description: Originally: no workflow ran on Windows, so no Windows path was ever exercised by automation. REQ-006 fixed a crash that occurred on every adapter timeout on Windows and it survived to be found by hand because nothing tested it. Closed 2026-09-14 except for one point. pr-check.yml is now a matrix over ubuntu-latest and windows-latest with fail-fast false and no continue-on-error, running the suite with -rs so each platform's skips appear with reasons, then tools/integrity.py -- which was verified on Windows first. Seven tests were added; four of them delete os.killpg so the taskkill fallback, unreachable on a machine that has process groups, is exercised on Linux too. Still pending: the run is non-advisory but not required, because this repository has no rulesets and main is unprotected, so no check is required at all. Making one required is a repository setting rather than a file and is the owner's call.
acceptance_criteria: a workflow runs the test suite on Windows/the run is required rather than advisory/the three currently skipped tests are accounted for as skipped-with-a-reason on each platform rather than silently absent
risk_notes: Adding a matrix to the nightly training workflow would double a two-hour job so the test run belongs in a separate fast workflow/Windows runners are slower and some adapter binaries are unavailable there so expect new legitimate skips

developer-tooling.title: Have OmniEngineering register and verify Arbiter's live MCP server
developer-tooling.description: omni doctor never checked that an assistant working in this repo could actually reach Arbiter as MCP tools -- there was no .mcp.json, and nothing in make_ai.py exercised the MCP server at all, only static text in files unrelated to it. Add .mcp.json registering `arbiter mcp` (stdio) as server "arbiter", and a doctor check (validate_mcp_server) that imports arbiter.mcp and calls _build_server() for real rather than grepping for file text, because the mcp SDK's own shape has moved under this project before (23bc43e, same day). Document in .ai/project-configuration.md that arbiter_scan/arbiter_gate/arbiter_review_queue should be called through MCP when available, with the CLI remaining the only way to run arbiter review --apply since no MCP tool records a verdict.
acceptance_criteria: .mcp.json registers an "arbiter" server running `arbiter mcp`
omni doctor's validate_mcp_server builds the live MCP server and fails if it cannot rather than only checking .mcp.json's text
.ai/project-configuration.md tells assistants to prefer the MCP tools over the CLI when they are available
validation_required: python omni doctor shows the new MCP check passing
risk_notes: the live check only passes when the optional mcp extra is installed; without it doctor warns instead of failing

developer-tooling.title: Stop vendored and generated content from being scanned as first-party source
developer-tooling.description: Scanning STEP-Migration and STEP_App as a system surfaced three compounding gaps that together reported a third-party library's own source as a leaked private key, and buried real findings under tens of thousands from vendored code. (1) _pem_has_key_material judged a PEM block real by checking whether any text after a BEGIN marker contained a colon anywhere in the next ~4000 characters -- a check meant to allow encrypted-key preambles (Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED), but satisfied by almost any surrounding prose or code, so ecdsa's own PEM-parsing source and packaging metadata were reported as committed keys. (2) inventory.classify()'s GENERATED_HINTS/IAC_HINTS hardcoded the literal name cdk.out, so a project using CDK_OUTDIR to redirect synth output to a renamed directory (cdk.out.chk, seen on the real system) fell through to role=source, and a branch-ordering bug meant that even the unrenamed case would have classified a CDK stack's own synthesized *.template.json as generated rather than the iac role that exempts nothing, losing the ground-truth scanning SKIP_DIRS says is deliberate. (3) bandit and checkov each walk {workdir} with their own traversal, independent of SKIP_DIRS, so both walked into a full vendored .venv and a Lambda asset bundle's dependencies regardless of role -- bandit alone produced 129,379 raw findings and consumed 669s of its 900s budget on one such tree.
acceptance_criteria: _pem_has_key_material walks forward line by line and stops at the first line that is not base64 or a Key: value header
so surrounding code or prose cannot manufacture a body
classify() recognises a CDK_OUTDIR-renamed cdk.out* directory and classifies its synthesized *.template.json as iac rather than letting the directory-wide generated match swallow it
bandit and checkov are invoked with exclusions mirroring inventory.SKIP_DIRS plus a CDK asset-bundle pattern
verified empirically against a real vendored tree rather than assumed from documentation
validation_required: python -m pytest tests/ -q is 421 passed 3 skipped 0 failed
a real cross-repo scan of STEP-Migration + STEP_App dropped from 3 critical / 6011 total findings to 0 critical / 1121 total
with 0 findings remaining inside a vendored asset bundle and bandit's runtime dropping from 669s to 4s
risk_notes: the bandit/checkov exclude patterns are a fixed list mirroring SKIP_DIRS rather than reading it programmatically
so the two lists can drift apart if SKIP_DIRS changes without the adapters being updated to match

developer-tooling.title: Fix MCP client tests reading pydantic alias names instead of the field names
developer-tooling.description: test_the_tool_schemas_still_build_against_the_installed_sdk and test_the_stdio_server_actually_starts_and_answers_a_real_client read .inputSchema, .serverInfo and .isError off objects the installed mcp SDK returns. Those models take a camelCase alias on construction but expose the field back out as the snake_case Python attribute via an alias generator, confirmed directly from Tool.model_fields/InitializeResult.model_fields/CallToolResult.model_fields on the installed SDK -- the camelCase name only exists on the wire. This was a pre-existing failure on main, unrelated to REQ-026, found while running the full suite during that work; confirmed by stashing REQ-026's changes and reproducing the same two failures against plain main.
acceptance_criteria: the two tests read .input_schema
.server_info and .is_error rather than the camelCase alias
python -m pytest tests/ -q shows 0 failed
validation_required: python -m pytest tests/ -q is 421 passed 3 skipped 0 failed

training-evidence.title: Cover the nightly training job with a requirement and a test
training-evidence.description: The nightly calibration job in .github/workflows/train.yml and tools/train_cycle.sh has never been covered by a requirement. Four defects were repaired in it on 2026-09-13 as unplanned work, including one where git add matched a gitignore entry, git exited 1, and bash -e failed the job two seconds after a 55-minute cycle finished successfully, so run 1 measured everything and committed nothing. A job that produces the project's only accumulating evidence and can fail silently after doing all its work needs owned acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: the job's outputs and the files it is expected to write back are stated as acceptance criteria/a failure to write back fails the job loudly rather than after the work is complete/the three accumulating files stay tracked while stamped per-run logs stay ignored/a test or a dry-run check covers the write-back path
risk_notes: The job runs for two hours nightly so a change to it cannot be validated quickly and a dry-run path is worth more than a live trial/It writes to the repository so a defect here can commit wrong evidence

legal.title: Establish licensing terms for arbiter
legal.description: Partly closed by engineering as of 2026-09-14; the remainder needs counsel and cannot be completed here. LICENSE exists at the repository root and pyproject.toml references it, copyright is asserted to Nicholas J Pauken, and LICENSE section 3 assigns scan output to the user -- the first three acceptance criteria. LICENSE is explicitly an interim notice and not the operative grant: it reserves all rights and grants none. The fourth criterion is L-6, the redistribution review for the five bundled analyzers, recorded in NOTICE.md with a date and a named reviewer. That is a legal determination about semgrep's LGPL-2.1 terms and it must not be signed by anyone who did not perform it, so this requirement stays pending until a person does. It blocks the air-gapped bundle and nothing else; docs/licensing.md records the open questions.
acceptance_criteria: a LICENSE file exists at the repository root and pyproject.toml references it
copyright ownership is asserted
ownership of scan output is assigned to the user
the redistribution review for bundled analyzers is recorded in NOTICE.md with a date and a reviewer
risk_notes: Requires qualified legal review and cannot be completed by engineering alone
the air-gapped bundle roadmap item stays blocked until the semgrep LGPL-2.1 redistribution question is answered
